claims.text: Machine-learning optimization of silicide coatings using oxidation-performance, formulation, and processing data will improve high-temperature oxidation resistance relative to conventional empirical optimization.
Refractory high-entropy alloys with unprotected surfaces can be susceptible to high-temperature oxidation degradation.
A Si-20Cr-20Fe formulation is an example of a silicide coating suitable for the proposed optimization approach.
A machine-learning framework can correlate coating composition and processing parameters with oxidation outcomes to optimize a silicide coating.
The proposed coating is intended for oxidative environments at approximately 1000°C or higher.
The optimized silicide coating will form a dense oxide scale.
The optimized silicide coating will form an adherent oxide scale.
A dense and adherent oxide scale limits oxygen ingress.
At high temperature, the silicide coating reacts to produce protective metal-silicate oxide layers.
The protective oxide layers act as a barrier to oxygen diffusion.
Restricting oxygen diffusion reduces oxidation kinetics.
ML-guided optimized coatings will reduce oxide-scale thickness relative to conventionally optimized silicide coatings.
ML-guided optimized coatings will improve oxidation resistance relative to conventionally optimized silicide coatings.
The proposed method may not apply to materials with different oxidation behavior or to non-metallic substrates.
Failure to achieve a statistically significant improvement, such as at least a 10% reduction in oxide-scale thickness or improved adhesion, under identical conditions would falsify the hypothesis.
